extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the AI Act establishes two main conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, and assessment of the quality management system plus technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII.

For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometric identification), the provider may choose internal control or a notified-body conformity assessment depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications under Articles 40/41 were applied.

For high-risk AI systems embedded in products already covered by existing EU harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I Section A, providers must follow the conformity assessment procedures of that legislation, with notified bodies additionally verifying compliance with AI-specific requirements.

A provider may generally choose any notified body for the Annex VII procedure, except that where the high-risk AI system is intended for use by law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities, or by Union institutions, the relevant market surveillance authority under Article 74(8) or (9) acts as the notified body.

A substantial modification to a high-risk AI system requires a new conformity assessment, unless the change falls within predetermined changes specified for systems that continue to learn after deployment.

Under Article 46, a market surveillance authority may, by derogation from Article 43 and upon justified request, authorise placing a specific high-risk AI system on the market without the standard conformity assessment, for a limited time, for exceptional reasons of public security, health, environmental protection, or protection of key infrastructure.

Under Annex VII point 4.5, where other means of verification prove insufficient, a notified body may, upon reasoned request, be granted access to the training data and trained models of the AI system, subject to existing IP and confidentiality protections.
Article 35 of the AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes the administrative framework for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies.
As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem specific to the AI Act is still being built, with designation processes ongoing across Member States and capacity described as limited.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act in the medical-device/SaMD context.

Notified bodies designated specifically under the AI Act are expected to begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments only after 2026, with interplay expected between these and existing MDR/IVDR notified-body assessments.

As of October 2025, the NANDO database lists 51 notified bodies designated under the Medical Devices Regulation (MDR) and 19 under the In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation (IVDR); these are not AI Act-specific designations.

The European Commission has proposed (COM(2025) 836, not yet confirmed as adopted) a new Annex XIV listing AI system categories/codes for the NANDO information system and amendments to Regulation (EU) 2018/1139, to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements and establish a framework for designating conformity assessment bodies.

A Council document (ST-7322-2026) lists specific AIP codes (e.g., AIP 0101–0105) corresponding to categories under Annex I of the AI Act, used to define the scope of designation of conformity assessment bodies referenced as notified under 'Article 30 of this Regulation'.

High-risk AI obligations under the AI Act, including the requirement to complete conformity assessment and obtain CE marking, are due to fully apply from August 2026 (cited variously as August 2, 2026).

Most high-risk AI systems not embedded in regulated products under Annex I can use the self-assessment Annex VI internal control route, while Annex VII third-party notified-body assessment is mandatory for biometric identification systems and certain systems treated as safety components under Annex I product regulations.

open_issues: No source dated after April 2026 states the current (as of October 2026) number or identity of notified bodies formally designated specifically under the AI Act, leaving the present designation status unclear.

It is unclear whether the Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) creating a new Annex XIV and NANDO codes for AI Act conformity assessment bodies, and the related Council document (ST-7322-2026) referencing 'Article 30 of this Regulation,' have been formally adopted or remain under negotiation.

The sources do not clarify how the numbering/structure of the proposed designation framework (e.g., 'Article 30' in source 8) relates to the adopted AI Act's own Article 35 framework for notified body lists.

No source explains in detail how providers of high-risk AI systems requiring notified-body assessment (Annex VII) are expected to comply given the apparent lack of designated AI Act-specific notified bodies as of early-to-mid 2026, beyond the limited Article 46 derogation route.

The relationship and transition process between existing MDR/IVDR-designated notified bodies and newly required AI Act-specific notified body designations for medical device AI systems is not fully detailed.
No source provides data on how many Article 46 derogations have actually been granted or how frequently this route has been used in practice.
report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act and the State of Notified Body Designation

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes a two-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems—internal control (Annex VI) or notified-body assessment (Annex VII)—with the applicable route depending on the system's category (high confidence). However, while the legal framework is well-defined, the practical infrastructure of notified bodies specifically designated under the AI Act appears, as of the most recent available sources (early-to-mid 2026), still under construction, with designation processes ongoing and, in at least the medical-device/SaMD context, no AI Act-specific notified bodies yet designated (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 establishes two main pathways for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, and assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)). Most high-risk systems not embedded in regulated products can use the self-assessment Annex VI route, while Annex VII third-party assessment is mandatory for biometric identification systems and certain safety-component systems under Annex I product regulations (low confidence) ([Quantamix](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment), [Openlayer](https://www.openlayer.com/blog/eu-ai-act-compliance-checklist-high-risk-systems)).

For Annex III point 1 biometric identification systems, providers may choose internal control or notified-body assessment depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications under Articles 40/41 were applied (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf)). For AI systems embedded in products already covered by EU harmonisation legislation (Annex I Section A), providers must follow that legislation's existing conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

### Notified Body Selection and Access
Providers may generally choose any notified body for the Annex VII procedure, except where the system is intended for use by law enforcement, immigration/asylum authorities, or EU institutions, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority under Article 74(8)/(9) acts as the notified body (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Under Annex VII point 4.5, notified bodies may, upon reasoned request and where other verification means are insufficient, gain access to training data and trained models, subject to IP and confidentiality protections (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Modifications and Derogations
A substantial modification to a high-risk AI system generally requires a new conformity assessment, unless the change falls within predetermined changes specified for continuously-learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Under Article 46, market surveillance authorities may, by derogation and for exceptional reasons (public security, health, environmental protection, critical infrastructure), authorise market placement without standard conformity assessment for a limited time (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)).

### State of Notified Body Designation
Article 35 establishes the administrative framework for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies (low confidence) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)). As of October 2025, NANDO listed 51 notified bodies under MDR and 19 under IVDR—these are existing medical-device designations, not AI Act-specific ones (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). As of March 2026, the notified-body ecosystem specific to the AI Act is still being built, with designation processes ongoing across Member States and capacity described as limited (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)). More narrowly, as of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act specifically in the medical-device/SaMD context (low confidence) ([AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)).

The Commission has proposed (COM(2025) 836, status unconfirmed) a new Annex XIV listing AI system categories/codes for the NANDO system, alongside amendments integrating AI Act requirements into aviation-sector regulation 2018/1139 (medium confidence) ([Council document](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)). A related Council document lists specific AIP codes (0101–0105) tied to Annex I categories, referencing designation under "Article 30" of an unspecified regulation, to define conformity assessment body scope (medium confidence) ([Council document](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). High-risk obligations, including conformity assessment and CE marking, are generally cited as applying from August 2, 2026 (low confidence) ([sota.io](https://sota.io/blog/eu-ai-act-eu-declaration-conformity-ce-marking-registration-saas-providers-2026)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
No direct contradictions were detected between sources. However, several claims carry low confidence (below 0.4) and should be treated cautiously: the characterization of the AI Act notified-body ecosystem as still under construction ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)), the narrower claim of zero designations in the medical-device/SaMD context ([AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)), the Article 35 characterization ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)), the August 2026 deadline citation, and the Annex III biometric-system route description. The relationship between the "Article 30" reference in the Council document and the adopted Act's Article 35 framework is unclear and may reflect differing drafts or numbering.

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear how many, if any, notified bodies have been formally designated specifically under the AI Act as of late 2026 beyond the medical-device context, and whether COM(2025) 836 has been adopted. The transition process between existing MDR/IVDR notified bodies and new AI Act-specific designations for medical-device AI is not detailed, nor is practical guidance for providers needing Annex VII assessment amid apparent designation gaps. Data on actual use of the Article 46 derogation route is absent.

# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act and the State of Notified Body Designation

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes a two-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems—internal control (Annex VI) or notified-body assessment (Annex VII)—with the applicable route depending on the system's category (high confidence). However, while the legal framework is well-defined, the practical infrastructure of notified bodies specifically designated under the AI Act appears, as of the most recent available sources (early-to-mid 2026), still largely under construction, with the Commission's supplementary designation framework not yet confirmed as formally adopted (low-to-medium confidence).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 establishes two main pathways for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, and assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)). Most high-risk systems not embedded in regulated products can use the self-assessment Annex VI route, while Annex VII third-party assessment is mandatory for biometric identification systems and certain safety-component systems under Annex I product regulations (low confidence) ([Quantamix](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment), [Openlayer](https://www.openlayer.com/blog/eu-ai-act-compliance-checklist-high-risk-systems)).

For Annex III point 1 biometric identification systems, providers may choose internal control or notified-body assessment depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications under Articles 40/41 were applied (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf)). For AI systems embedded in products already covered by EU harmonisation legislation (Annex I Section A), providers must follow that legislation's existing conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

### Notified Body Selection and Access
Providers may generally choose any notified body for the Annex VII procedure, except where the system is intended for use by law enforcement, immigration/asylum authorities, or EU institutions, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority under Article 74(8)/(9) acts as the notified body (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Under Annex VII point 4.5, notified bodies may, upon reasoned request and where other verification means are insufficient, gain access to training data and trained models, subject to IP and confidentiality protections (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Modifications and Derogations
A substantial modification to a high-risk AI system generally requires a new conformity assessment, unless the change falls within predetermined changes specified for continuously-learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Under Article 46, market surveillance authorities may, by derogation and for exceptional reasons (public security, health, environmental protection, critical infrastructure), authorise market placement without standard conformity assessment for a limited time (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)).

### State of Notified Body Designation
Article 35 establishes the administrative framework for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies (low confidence) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)). As of October 2025, NANDO listed 51 notified bodies under MDR and 19 under IVDR—these are existing medical-device designations, not AI Act-specific ones (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). As of March–April 2026, sources indicate the AI Act-specific notified body ecosystem remains under construction, with no bodies formally designated for AI Act purposes, including in the medical-device/SaMD context (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)).

The Commission has proposed (COM(2025) 836, status unconfirmed) a new Annex XIV listing AI system categories/codes for the NANDO system, alongside amendments integrating AI Act requirements into aviation-sector regulation 2018/1139 (medium confidence) ([Council document](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)). A related Council document lists specific AIP codes (0101–0105) tied to Annex I categories, referencing designation under "Article 30" of an unspecified regulation, to define conformity assessment body scope (medium confidence) ([Council document](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). High-risk obligations, including conformity assessment and CE marking, are generally cited as applying from August 2, 2026 (low confidence) ([sota.io](https://sota.io/blog/eu-ai-act-eu-declaration-conformity-ce-marking-registration-saas-providers-2026)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
No direct contradictions were detected between sources. However, several claims carry low confidence (below 0.4) and should be treated cautiously: the status of notified body designation as of 2026 ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act); [AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)), the Article 35 characterization ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)), the August 2026 deadline citation, and the Annex III biometric-system route description. The relationship between the "Article 30" reference in the Council document and the adopted Act's Article 35 framework is unclear and may reflect differing drafts or numbering.

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear how many, if any, notified bodies have been formally designated specifically under the AI Act as of late 2026, and whether COM(2025) 836 has been adopted. The transition process between existing MDR/IVDR notified bodies and new AI Act-specific designations for medical-device AI is not detailed, nor is practical guidance for providers needing Annex VII assessment amid apparent designation gaps. Data on actual use of the Article 46 derogation route is absent.
